paragraphs: Rabbi Yose bar Assi: Mekhilta, Yitro, parashah BaChodesh, chapter 3.[^2]
Rabbi Yaakov bar Assi: Yelamdenu, beginning of Pekudei.

notes.text: The linked Gemara calls him Rav Chiyya bar Assi, whom the elders recall making an eruv for the entire city. [Heilprin’s Chiyya entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1229&lang=en) cites the same folio.

The [Vilna 1884 annotations on Lekach Tov](https://www.sefaria.org/Notes_and_Corrections_on_Midrash_Lekach_Tov%2C_Exodus.24.9) quote Mekhilta, Yitro 3, with Rabbi Yose berabbi Assi, as listed by [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1940&lang=en). The annotations also report Yishmael berabbi Yose from Yalkut and have Yose berabbi Yehudah in their base text, as does the linked [Beeri Mekhilta](https://www.sefaria.org/Mekhilta_DeRabbi_Yishmael%2C_Tractate_Bachodesh.3.3). In [Tanchuma, Pekudei 2:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Midrash_Tanchuma%2C_Pekudei.2.3), the Hebrew names Rabbi Yaakov berabbi Assi and the English gives Issi. [Heilprin’s Yaakov entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2126&lang=en) cites Yelamdenu. These notices leave open whether the fathers were the same person.
